Whether cookie isolation must be host-only or restricted to Registry's HTTPS origin
dispositions.what: The owner interface's own host name: the deployment gives the owner interface a host name under which no other HTTPS service of the same host answers (on the home server not the kernel workplace, the gateway or PresuPro), so no other service receives the host-only owner session cookie; Registry cannot check it. Decided on 2026-11-25 under the owner's direction of 2026-11-24 (data-protection matrix row P6), option 2 of the round; the owner may reverse it. The deployment step belongs to the Factory's platform deployment.
keeps: to the owner interface's host name: the cookie is host-only, set without
options: Change the guarantee to Registry's host and require deployment isolation from other same-host services.
Require a dedicated owner-interface host name.
Choose a session transport with origin-level scoping.
consequences: The choice determines whether another HTTPS service on the same host may receive the session credential.

dispositions.topic_text: Deployment component and check guaranteeing remote HTTPS-only owner access
dispositions.what: Where TLS is terminated for remote owner access and the deployment check that no plaintext remote route bypasses it (Registry's own TLS, a VPN-restricted reverse proxy, or an HTTPS-only VPN gateway); every option keeps: reached from another machine, the owner interface is reachable only through HTTPS and only over the owner's VPN (A13 rule 1, A17 rule 1, R0-29, R0-48).
keeps:
Reached from
another machine, the interface is reachable only through HTTPS;
options: Registry terminates TLS directly.
A VPN-restricted reverse proxy terminates TLS and isolates Registry's backend listener.
An HTTPS-only VPN gateway exposes the interface.
consequences: Any proxy or gateway choice must prove that no remote plaintext route bypasses it.

dispositions.topic_text: Required tests covering every stored required value
dispositions.what: How completely the bound checks show the invariant — every conjunct, case and action the rule covers — is judged on the tests' code at State 8 (witness_material) and carried to the Factory checks issue; State 2 only says what must be shown (owner, 2026-11-24).
keeps: for every stored required value v: v present and strip(v) != ""   -- A02-2
options: Extend the Required test across every required field.
Split the invariant and add tests for the uncovered fields.
Carry a universal structural assertion only after State 7 while retaining explicit State 2 cases.
consequences: Without coverage, a generated implementation can omit the required-address check while every named test passes.

dispositions.topic_text: Required test covering the complete rights matrix for every service and operation
dispositions.what: How completely the bound checks show the invariant — every conjunct, case and action the rule covers — is judged on the tests' code at State 8 (witness_material) and carried to the Factory checks issue; State 2 only says what must be shown (owner, 2026-11-24).
keeps: call(op) with token of service s accepted => op in rights(s)   -- A09-1
options: Add a generated exhaustive service-operation matrix test.
State an independent universal assertion over the release rights table.
Narrow the invariant, which would weaken the accepted denial-by-default requirement.
consequences: Without universal coverage, an undeclared operation may be accepted by one service.

dispositions.topic_text: Failure injection point proving pointer supersession and replacement are one transaction
dispositions.what: Where a test makes the publish transaction fail — after the old pointer is written superseded and before the new one is stored, or after the new one's write while uncommitted — so that a separate-commit implementation is told apart; How completely the bound checks show the invariant — every conjunct, case and action the rule covers — is judged on the tests' code at State 8 (witness_material) and carried to the Factory checks issue; State 2 only says what must be shown (owner, 2026-11-24).
keeps:
publish(p, t) accepted => the previous published pointer of p, t becomes
superseded in the same transaction as the new one is stored   -- A07-4
options: Fail after writing the old pointer as superseded but before storing the new pointer.
Fail after attempting the new-pointer write while the transaction remains uncommitted.
consequences: A failure before both writes cannot distinguish transactional atomicity from separate later commits.

dispositions.topic_text: Exact class-check test-release fixtures and altered class-table rows
dispositions.what: The test release's exact fixture rows for A09 rule 4 (a service's highest class lowered below an answer, or a Kernel-reachable field classed personal_data); every option keeps: an answer above the token's highest class is refused whole, and the production release's tables are unchanged.
keeps:
An answer that would carry a class above the
   token's highest is refused whole; Registry never answers part of it.
options: Lower a selected service's highest-class row below an existing answer.
Classify a Kernel-reachable answer field as personal_data while retaining Kernel's ceiling.
consequences: The Factory must construct a test release without changing the production release's policy.

dispositions.topic_text: Factory mechanism for inducing cleanup removal failure after successful store creation
dispositions.what: How the Factory makes the removal of a store a failed start made new fail while its making succeeds (targeted filesystem fault, structural check of the cleanup branch); every option keeps A17 rule 2: one it cannot remove is an empty store of the release's version, which the next start opens.
keeps:
one it cannot remove is an empty store of the release's version, which the
   next start opens as any store.
options: Inject a targeted filesystem removal failure.
Inspect the generated cleanup branch structurally.
Use platform-specific permission fault injection.
consequences: The chosen check must allow store creation and fail only the later cleanup removal.

dispositions.topic_text: Factory proof that the snapshot instant is taken at the first snapshot-fixing read
dispositions.what: How the Factory shows that a backup's instant is read at the read that fixes its snapshot (instrumented clock and store, a structurally approved snapshot path, or both); every option keeps A18 rule 1: the instant is that of the first read of the copy's transaction.
options: Instrument clock and store calls with distinct readings.
Require a structurally approved snapshot-opening path.
Combine structural enforcement with an ordering test.
consequences: The Factory must distinguish a clock read at snapshot fixation from a later read.

dispositions.topic_text: Factory verification that all agent-authority flows share the required serialization boundary
dispositions.what: How the Factory checks that every agent-authority call and every change of its session are applied one at a time (structural call-graph and transaction-scope check, controlled concurrency, or both); every option keeps A10 rule 6.
keeps:
A call and every change of its session — a revocation, an archiving, the
   session's end — are applied one at a time: a call whose transaction
   commits before the change is accepted, one that commits after it is
   checked against the changed session and refused when the change removed
   its right.
options: Structural call-graph and transaction-scope checking.
Controlled concurrency instrumentation.
Both structural and behavioral checks.
consequences: A structural check covers future operations; a race check demonstrates the ordering behavior.

dispositions.topic_text: Factory control point proving overlapping publications and both serialization orders
dispositions.what: The control point by which a check makes two publications or withdrawals of one project overlap and shows both orders (lock barrier, lock instrumentation, deterministic transaction backend), adding no product operation; every option keeps A07: each runs on the result of the one before, in the order of the store's write lock.
keeps:
Every publish and every withdrawal on one project's pointers is
   serialised with the others: each runs on the result of the one before, in
   the order their transactions take the store's one write lock, which is
   also the order they commit in;
options: Inject a Factory-only lock barrier.
Instrument lock acquisition.
Use a deterministic fake transaction backend.
consequences: The check must demonstrate genuine overlap and both serialization orders without adding a product operation.

dispositions.topic_text: Factory verification of exclusive secret-generation and comparison routing
dispositions.what: How the Factory checks that every secret comparison goes through random_values.equal_in_constant_time and every secret value through random_values.make_secret_value, and that none reaches a URL, log, diagnostic or audit entry (static call-graph and forbidden-call checks, runtime substitution, or both); every option keeps A13 rule 7.
keeps:
each is compared
   in constant time and never appears in a URL, a log line, a diagnostic or an
   audit entry (R0-29, R0-37).
options: Static forbidden-call and call-graph checks.
Runtime substitution of the approved functions.
Both static and focused runtime checks.
consequences: Static coverage is needed to include indirect and future generated call sites.

dispositions.topic_text: Whether A02 test 5 uses one multi-error request or two separate requests
dispositions.what: Whether A02 test 5's fixture uses one request with both invalid values or separate requests plus a multi-error case; every option keeps A04 rule 6: every failing check of one stage is named, and no valid or absent value is.
keeps:
When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of
   them.
options: Use one request containing both invalid values.
Use separate cases plus an additional multi-error assertion.
consequences: The Factory fixture must not expect a refusal to name a value that was valid or absent.
